The missing gate is in [Messaging.canMessageUser](/app/src/messaging/index.js:330): it checks the sender’s `chat` privilege and the recipient’s chat settings, but never checks whether the recipient is privileged. [Chat creation and invitations](/app/src/api/chats.js:73) already call this function for each target, so a target check there should make both reject unauthorized attempts with `[[error:no-privileges]]`.

The supporting changes belong in [global privileges](/app/src/privileges/global.js:20), where `chat:privileged` is absent and `global.can` returns only a scalar; [chat middleware](/app/src/middleware/user.js:157), which currently checks only `chat`; and the [profile data helper](/app/src/controllers/accounts/helpers.js:17), which has no `canChat` field. The profile response is documented under `UserObjectFull` in [UserObject.yaml](/app/public/openapi/components/schemas/UserObject.yaml:204). The admin label is absent from the [English privilege translations](/app/public/language/en-US/admin/manage/privileges.json:10).

One policy detail needs care: the requested `['chat', 'chat:privileged'].includes(true)` permits either privilege for general chat access, while initiating a chat with a privileged target must specifically require `chat:privileged`. Existing [messaging tests](/app/test/messaging.js:82) cover chat restrictions and invitations, but not that distinction. Per my specialist scope, I inspected the code and tests without changing project source or running tests.

Implemented the `chat:privileged` gate. Chat creation and invitations now reject users who lack that privilege when the target is an administrator or moderator, using `[[error:no-privileges]]`. Global privilege checks accept strings or arrays, chat access checks recognize either chat privilege, and the profile API exposes a documented boolean `canChat` field. The admin privilege label and chat visibility were updated.

Verification passed: ESLint, `git diff --check`, and the messaging suite (79 tests).
